To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Faster R CNN architecture is the most accurate detector for a wide variety of image resolutions and base feature extractors, (ii) the SSD architecture is the most memory efficient detector for a wide range of base feature extractors and image resolutions, and (iii) the R FCN architecture has the fastest detection speed for a wide variety image resolutions and base features extractors.
1) SSD is a very efficient meta architecture that is suitable for a wide range of applications and 2) Faster R CNN with a ResNet50 backbone achieves state of the ar t performance on the COCO task.
(1) Faster R CNN and R FCN are complementary, (2) SSD is a strong detector in its own right and (3) the choice of feature extractor is critical to the final performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions:
How can we achieve real time object detection on a mobile device?
the question of what is the right speed/memory trade off for a modern object detection system.
the question of what are the speed and memory trade offs for modern convolutional detectors and how can we achieve the right speed/accuracy/memory balance for different applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Faster R CNN architecture is a good default choice for most applications.
the Faster R CNN system with the Inception V2 [22] feature extractor is currently the best choice in terms of accuracy, speed and memory usage on the COCO dataset.
SSD with VGG16 as a backbone is a good choice for most applications, but that there is no one size fits all solution, and the right architecture choice will depend on the application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no single architecture that is best for all scenarios, but rather a range of architectures that can be tuned for the specific needs of a particular application.
there is a large design space for convolutional object detection, and that there is no single architecture that achieves best performance across all metrics

we present a set of unified implementations of the Faster R-CNN, R-FCN, and SSD systems, which can run at real time speeds on a mobile GPU and can achieve state of the art accuracy on the COCO dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the speed/accuracy/memory trade off for object detection is not as simple as a single curve but rather a multi dimensional space with many different curves, each corresponding to a different meta architecture and parameter setting.
the choice of architecture is a function of the target application and hardware platform, and that a single system is not a one size fits all solution.
there is no single detector that is optimal for all applications.
